messages:
IncidentBot: AUTOPAGE fired for service= inference-gateway-eu1 — alert=high_5xx_rate — threshold breached (1m)
PagerDuty: Page INC-7891 -> @oncall-sre rotated, escalation policy=critical-runtime
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: new incident created: https://pd.example.com/incidents/INC-7891
Ashok (oncall): acked. I'm on it, grabbing context. :rotating_light:
Laura (SRE): I see the spike in error-rate across eu-west1 -> 5xx rate went from 0.7% to ~8% at 00:05 UTC, p95 latency also up. Dashboards: https://grafana.example.com/d/inf/gateway-eu1
James (runtime): Logs show a flood of connection reset errors to redis-cluster-primary and a jump in kv-cache-miss. Sample error:
```
ERROR inference-gateway: upstream "redis://10.2.1.3:6379" connection reset by peer\ntrace_id=abcd1234
```
Maya (eng-runtime): timeline: we rolled a small canary of inference-gateway:v2-canary-20260315 at 00:02 UTC (5% traffic). Canary changed keepalive settings and connection pool tuning.
Ashok (oncall): hypothesis: canary introduced a keepalive change that interacts badly with redis leader and causes resets -> backend errors bubble up as 5xx. Will remove canary weight and scale warm pool.
Ashok (oncall): immediate mitigation steps I will run: 1) shift traffic off canary, 2) scale gateway replicas, 3) disable client-side retries to avoid retry storms, 4) enable fallback routing to warm inference pool.
Ashok (oncall): running helm patch to set canary weight to 0:
```
helm upgrade inference-gateway ./chart --set canary.weight=0 --namespace prod-eu
```
Laura (SRE): also bumping gateway replicas from 6 -> 12 in eu cluster while we stabilize:
```
kubectl -n prod-eu scale deploy inference-gateway --replicas=12
```
James (runtime): applying short-lived circuit breaker on redis client to fail fast (reduce cascade). Patch applied to config map `gateway-conn`.
Maya (eng-runtime): I'm toggling retries down to 0 on the proxy layer to prevent amplified traffic:
```
kubectl -n prod-eu patch configmap proxy-config -p '{"data":{"retries":"0"}}'
```
PagerDuty: Incident INC-7891 acknowledged by Ashok (oncall) at 00:07 UTC
Ashok (oncall): monitoring metrics... will update in 2m.
Laura (SRE): customer impact: estimated ~8% of requests in EU region got 5xx during spike window. Erroring requests mainly short chat sessions; preliminary list of affected tenants being compiled. (Kendra, please prep CS outreach for top 3 paying EU customers).
Kendra (CS): Roger, preparing templated note and pinging account teams. ETA 10m.
SRE-Shift-Bot: traffic reweighting to canary=0 completed by Ashok at 00:09 UTC.
Ashok (oncall): replicas scaled, retries set to 0, circuit breaker enabled. I'm seeing 5xx trend down from 8% -> 1.2% over the last 4 minutes.
James (runtime): root-level clue: redis leader reported a small GC and transient connection churn around 00:03 UTC; keepalive change increased idle-connection churn -> resets. We should correlate with redis metrics (conn_count, tcp_rst).
Maya (eng-runtime): rolling the canary back fully and will open a follow-up pull request with adjusted keepalive defaults and a compat test against redis cluster.
Ashok (oncall): handing off to Laura for postmortem and follow-up actions. I'll remain available if needed.
Laura (SRE): taking the handoff. Opening incident ticket INC-7891-postmortem and adding action items: 1) revert keepalive change or add redis compatibility config, 2) add canary e2e that simulates redis load and idle timeouts, 3) add alert for KV cache miss spike earlier than 5xx, 4) craft customer comms.
Kendra (CS): outreach sent to accounts 90m later, will attach timeline once draft is complete.
Ashok (oncall): final check: error-rate steady at ~0.6% (back to baseline). PD incident set to resolved by Ashok at 00:15 UTC. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident INC-7891 marked resolved — automated entry: duration ~13m — primary cause: canary keepalive/connect tuning incompatible with current redis leader behavior (transient conn churn) -> upstream 5xx cascade.
Laura (SRE): will track RCA and remediation in the postmortem. Thanks team for quick actions. :white_check_mark:
